HOW MACHINES LEARN
Three types of machine learning
DATA HAS 2 PARTS
Attributes
The info we give the model to make its guess
Labels
The result we expect the model to give
ATTRIBUTES
LABEL
area
rooms
city
price
900
2
Pune
₹60L
WITH A TEACHER
Supervised
Learns from attributes and their labels (the right answers).
e.g. Photos labelled "cat" or "dog" → it learns to spot cats.
NO TEACHER
Unsupervised
Only attributes, no labels. Finds groups and patterns on its own.
e.g. Grouping shoppers by what they buy.
TRIAL & ERROR
Reinforcement
Learns by trying things and getting rewards or penalties.
e.g. A game AI gets points for winning and learns to win more.

EXAMPLE · GUESS A HOUSE PRICE

Guess: ₹50 lakh
Actual: ₹60 lakh (off by 10)

input → neuron → output

AI & LLMs for Beginners
11
DEEP LEARNING
Activation function: what comes out
Data
numbers in
→
Math sum
add them up
→
Activation
pick output type
→
Output
the answer
Tanh
Turns any number into −1 to 1.
Good for: older networks
ReLU
Below 0 becomes 0. Above 0 stays.
Good for: hidden layers
Sigmoid
Turns any number into 0 to 1.
Good for: yes or no
Softmax
Turns scores into % that add to 100.
Good for: pick one answer
Activation function = decides what type of output a neuron makes.
Simple tip: hidden layers use ReLU. The last layer depends on the question.

DEEP LEARNING
What is deep learning?
Stack the neurons and layers we just met and you get a neural network.
Input layer
The numbers we feed in, e.g. pixels.
Hidden layers
Where the work happens. Deep = many hidden layers.
Output layer
The answer, e.g. cat or dog.
Weights
Every line. Learning = adjusting them.
AI & LLMs for Beginners
13
DEEP LEARNING
Why GPUs? Lots of small maths at once
CPU
a few powerful cores
Like a few expert chefs: great at complex tasks, one after another.
GPU
thousands of small cores
Like a stadium of helpers: each does one simple sum, all at the same time.
Training = millions of tiny multiply-and-add sums.
They don't depend on each other, so a GPU can do them in parallel. That's why AI runs on GPUs.

HOW LLMS WORK · STEP 1
Embeddings: words become numbers
I love apples
↓ SPLIT INTO TOKENS
I
love
apples
↓ EACH TOKEN → A LIST OF NUMBERS
0.24 0.31 0.43
0.23 0.45 0.07
0.12 0.67 0.89
1
Computers only understand numbers.
2
So each word becomes a list of numbers that holds its meaning.
3
Similar words get similar numbers: apple ≈ banana.
Problem: one word always gets the same numbers.
"Apple" the fruit and "Apple" the company look identical. We need context.
AI & LLMs for Beginners
18
HOW LLMS WORK · STEP 2
Positional encoding: keeping word order
THE PROBLEM
The cat chased the mouse.
The mouse chased the cat.
The model reads all words at once, so both look like the same bag of words:
{ the, cat, chased, mouse }
THE FIX
Give every word a position stamp, added to its numbers.
The
#1
cat
#2
chased
#3
the
#4
mouse
#5
Now "cat at #2" and "cat at #5" look different.
Word meaning + word position = what the model actually reads.
The first Transformers used sine and cosine waves for this. Newer models use tricks like RoPE.

HOW LLMS WORK
Why attention: meaning comes from context
BEFORE ATTENTION
"Apple"
Fixed meaning. Same numbers in every sentence.
Tech 40%
Apple
Fruit 40%
↓
Attention reads the words around it:
I love Apple phones
AFTER ATTENTION
"Apple" + phones
"Phones" pulls Apple towards tech.
Tech 80%
Apple
Fruit 20%
Attention turns a fixed meaning into a meaning that fits the sentence.
Consider a plain sentence : I love Apple
HOW LLMS WORK · STEP 3
Attention: which words matter to each other
I
love
apples
I
1.0
0.7
0.2
love
0.6
1.0
0.8
apples
0.4
0.9
1.0
Darker = the two words are more closely linked
1
Every word looks at every other word, all at once.
2
Each pair gets a score: high = closely related.
3
Now "apples" next to "love" clearly means the fruit.
Old models read one word at a time. Transformers read the whole sentence at once.
Attention is the heart of the Transformer, the "T" in ChatGPT.
AI & LLMs for Beginners
20
HOW LLMS WORK · STEP 4
Why one attention isn't enough
ONE SENTENCE, TWO MEANINGS
"She saw a man with a telescope"
MEANING A
She saw a man holding a telescope.
link: man ↔ telescope
MEANING B
She used the telescope to see him.
link: she ↔ telescope
One attention can only focus on a few links at a time.
So the model uses many attentions, called heads, each looking for a different kind of link.
AI & LLMs for Beginners
21
HOW LLMS WORK · STEP 5
Multi-head attention: teamwork
Back to the telescope sentence. Every head reads it, but each looks for a different link.
HEAD 1
Who did what?
She saw a man with a telescope
Links "she" (the doer) to "man" (who she saw).
HEAD 2 · MEANING A
Who had it?
She saw a man with a telescope
Links "man" to "telescope": he was holding it.
HEAD 3 · MEANING B
How did she see?
She saw a man with a telescope
Links "she" to "telescope": she used it.
COMBINE
Join all heads → the model sees every link at once.
final = original + mix(heads)

HOW LLMS WORK
How ChatGPT-style models are made
1
Pre-training
Read a huge library of text and practise predicting the next token.
→ Base model: knows a lot, but just continues text.
→
2
Fine-tuning
Train on examples of good questions and answers written by people.
→ Follows instructions.
→
3
Human feedback
People rate answers. The model learns which are helpful and safe.
→ Chat model, e.g. ChatGPT
LIKE A NEW EMPLOYEE
Reads everything → gets job training → learns from the manager's feedback

USING LLMS WELL
Context window and temperature
SHORT-TERM MEMORY
Context window
Everything the model can see at once: your messages, its replies and any files.
← too old: forgotten
what it can see
Measured in tokens. Past the limit, the oldest text drops out.
CREATIVITY DIAL
Temperature
How adventurous the model is when it picks the next word.
Low · predictable
High · creative
Low: "The sky is blue."
High: "The sky is a sleepy ocean."
Low for facts and code. High for ideas and stories.

25
USING LLMS WELL
Prompting basics: a recipe
R
Role
Who should the AI be?
C
Context
What background does it need?
T
Task
Exactly what should it do?
F
Format
How should the answer look?
✗ VAGUE PROMPT
Write about AI.
✓ CLEAR PROMPT
You are a friendly teacher. My students are 15 and new to tech. Explain what AI is with 3 everyday examples. Use short bullet points, under 100 words.
Not happy? Reply and refine. It's a conversation, not a search box.
AI & LLMs for Beginners
26
USING LLMS WELL
Limits: where LLMs go wrong
01
Hallucinations
Can invent facts that sound confident. Check anything important.
02
Bias
Learns unfair patterns from the text it was trained on.
03
Outdated knowledge
Only knows what it read up to its training cut-off date.
04
Privacy
Never paste passwords, personal data or company secrets.
Use AI as a smart assistant, not the final judge.
